passages.provision_quote: (b) without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record
passages.note: The bill guarantees parental access to the education record and requires parental consent to change the record's gender identity, but its object is the record, not staff use of names or pronouns (rung 5) nor a duty to notify or answer on request about identity (rungs 3-4), so it shows only the parent-informed side.
House final passage vote, Maloy Yea; 6 Nays of 75 members is under 10%, so the vote is near-unanimous and cannot carry a chair alone.

rows.reasoning: Maloy voted Yea on S.B. 100 (2023), which bars a school from shielding a student's education record from parents and requires written parental consent to change the record's gender identity. That places him on the side of informing parents, but the bill's object is the education record, not "Require parental permission before staff use a different name or pronouns" or a duty to "notify parents", and the 59-6 vote is near-unanimous, so no single rung is established.
